title: The four titration curves
caption: 25.0 cm³ of 0.100 mol dm⁻³ acid titrated with 0.100 mol dm⁻³ base. Every curve reaches equivalence at 25.0 cm³, but where the pH jumps, and by how much, depends on whether acid and base are strong or weak. A weak acid with a weak base gives no sharp jump.
alt: Four titration curves: strong–strong jumps from about 3 to 11; weak acid–strong base from about 7 to 11; strong acid–weak base from about 3 to 7; weak–weak rises gradually through 7.
description: Strong acid + strong base: starts at pH 1, vertical section from about 3.4 to 10.6, equivalence at pH 7.
Weak acid + strong base: starts near pH 3, vertical section from about 7 to 10.6, equivalence about pH 8.7.
Strong acid + weak base: starts at pH 1, vertical section from about 3.4 to 6.6, equivalence about pH 5.3.
Weak acid + weak base: no vertical section.
